title: Long-term follow-up for bimanual microincision cataract surgery: comparison of results obtained by surgeons in training and experienced surgeons

license.statement: CC BY-NC 3.0 via Dove Medical Press terms (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution - Non Commercial (unported, v3.0) License); not CC BY or CC0, so the record is private

indication: Age-related cataract LOCS III grade 2-3; previous surgery, complicated cataract, uveitis, glaucoma, corneal opacity, mydriasis below 4 mm and ECD below 1500 cells/mm2 excluded; some patients contributed both eyes

groups.description: Group A: bimanual microincision cataract surgery (B-MICS, two 1.4 mm incisions, stop-and-chop, Akreos MI60 IOL) by three surgeons in training on their first B-MICS cases under expert supervision; 80 eyes of 62 patients
Group B: the same B-MICS technique by three experienced surgeons (the article's comparison group); 80 eyes of 59 patients

series.baseline_label: Preoperative endothelial count of the operated eye (Table 1 column 'Preoperative'; Konan Noncon Robo specular microscopy)
series.notes: Table 1 (Group A) row 'Endothelial count (cells/mm2)'; footnote: mean ± standard deviation; thousands separators removed by the record builder. All Group A surgeries had an 18-month follow-up (Methods); per-visit n not tabulated.

series.baseline_label: Preoperative endothelial count of the operated eye (Table 2 column 'Preoperative'; Konan Noncon Robo specular microscopy)
series.notes: Table 2 (Group B) row 'Endothelial count (cells/mm2)'; footnote: mean ± standard deviation; thousands separators removed by the record builder. Per-visit n not tabulated.

exclusions.what: Tables 1 and 2 BCVA, astigmatism and pachymetry rows
Mean endothelial cell loss and its range at 18 months (Results text)
exclusions.reason: Text values; the tabulated absolute ECD series are used

exclusions.what: Table 5 iris-prolapse subgroups of Group A
exclusions.reason: Groups defined by an intraoperative event and reported only for incision geometry, not ECD

notes: The groups differ by surgeon experience with the same standard technique, not by an investigational agent, device or technique variant: both are control-role, separate groups.
Patients with ocular pathology unrelated to surgery during follow-up were excluded from the cohort (Methods).
